GRAP 3 restrictions in Delhi: What is allowed and what is not
 GRAP Stage III is invoked when the Delhi air quality index (AQI) is between 301 and 400.
 Updated - November 06, 2026 05:35 pm IST 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Representational Image
 | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma
 The air quality in Delhi has deteriorated into the ‘severe’ category, with the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) imposing Stage III of the Graded Action Plan or GRAP due to the dangerous levels of air pollution in the national capital.
 What is GRAP?
 Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) is a set of emergency measures that kicks in to prevent further deterioration of air quality once it reaches a certain threshold.
 The first stage, GRAP-1, kicks in when the AQI is between 201 and 300 (Poor); the second stage, GRAP-2, is invoked when the AQI is between 301 and 400 (Very Poor); GRAP-3 kicks in between 401 and 500 (Severe); and GRAP-4 is invoked when the AQI is more than 450 (Severe+).
 What is not allowed?
 Here’s what’s not allowed under GRAP Stage III in the National Capital Region
 Construction and demolition activities  
 Strict restrictions are enforced on dust-generating C&D activities across the entire National Capital Region. This includes: 
  Earthwork for excavation and filing, including boring and drilling works.  
 Piling works and all demolition 
 Laying of sewer lines, water lines, drainage, and electric cables using an open trench system. 
 Brick and masonry works  
 Operation of RMC batching plants 
 Major welding and gas-cutting operations. 
 Painting, polishing, and varnishing works 
 Cement, plaster, and other coatings except for minor indoor repairs and maintenance 
 Cutting, grinding, and fixing of tiles, stones, and other floor materials, except for minor indoor repairs and maintenance.  
 Major road construction activities and repairs 
 Transfer, loading, or unloading of dust-generating materials anywhere within or outside project sites 
 Movement of vehicles carrying construction materials and waste on unpaved roads 
 Industrial and mining operations  
 Stone crushers must not be operated across the entire NCR 
 All mining and associated activities in the entire NCR must be closed down 
 Vehicle restrictions 
 NCR governments must restrict the plying of vehicles with BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel (or below) Light Motor Vehicles in Delhi and some districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad, and Gautam Buddha Nagar with high vehicle density 
 Delhi government must impose strict restrictions on plying of Delhi-registered diesel-operated BS-IV and below Medium Good Vehicles in Delhi 
 Diesel-operated BS-IV and below MGVs and Light Goods Vehicles registered outside Delhi are not permitted to enter 
 Heating 
 The use of coal and wood for heating purposes is prohibited. 
 What is permitted or regulated?
 Minor welding activities for mechanical, electrical, and plumbing works are permitted 
 Repairing of potholes is permitted 
 All construction and demolition activities other than the restricted dust-generating categories are permitted if they are relatively less polluting or less dust-generating subject to strict dust and waste management rules 
 Construction and demolition activities (under strict compliance) for railways, metro rail services, airport and inter-state bus terminals, national security, defence, projects of national importance, hospitals, highways, roads, flyovers, overbridges, power transmission, pipelines, and telecommunication services and sanitation projects are permitted 
 State governments of NCR and the Delhi government must conduct classes for children up to Class V in hybrid mode, offering online and physical classes wherever feasible 
 NCR governments and the Delhi government may take a call on allowing public, municipal, and private offices to work at 50% strength with the rest working from home.  
 Advisory to citizens to help reduce pollution
 Walk or use cycles for small distances 
 Choose a cleaner transport mode to commute 
 Combine short journeys and reduce trips 
 Postpone gatherings that increase traffic and outdoor exposure 
 Do not use coal and wood for heating purposes 
 Follow hybrid mode for primary schools and work-from-home when instructed
